name: Hofgarten Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Hofgarten in Innsbruck: A ten-hectare protected heritage landscape garden beside the Old Town, featuring centuries-old trees and a historic palm house.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Innsbrucker Hofgarten (Court Garden) is a protected ten-hectare public park located in the heart of Tyrol's capital, directly adjacent to the Imperial Hofburg, the Tyrolean State Theatre, and the Congress centre. Originally established in the early 15th century by Archduke Frederick IV as a princely garden, it was transformed into a formal baroque park under Empress Maria Theresa, before being redesigned in the mid-19th century into its present English landscape layout. Today, it serves as a serene green sanctuary where imperial heritage meets dramatic views of the towering Nordkette mountain range.

Route & Requirements

A stroll along the meandering pathways takes visitors past tranquil ponds, manicured seasonal flower displays, and an exceptional botanical collection of over 1,700 trees and shrubs. Several ancient specimens—including colossal beeches, plane trees, and oaks—date back more than two centuries, some reputedly planted by Empress Maria Theresa herself. Architectural highlights include the historic Music Pavilion, which hosts popular open-air summer concerts, and the lively outdoor giant chess boards that have drawn local players for generations. On the northern boundary stands the heritage-listed Palm House (Palmenhaus), a beautiful glasshouse structure home to an extensive botanical collection of over 1,700 tropical and subtropical plants, including rare palms, tree ferns, and exotic orchids. For families, an expansive adventure playground nestled in mature shade offers ample room for play.

Visit & Arrival

The Hofgarten is open daily year-round with free public admission. The gates open at 06:00 and close at dusk depending on the season (until 21:00 in midsummer, 17:30 in winter). The Palm House is open Monday through Friday from 09:00 to 17:00 (free admission). Arriving by car: located in the pedestrian-friendly city centre, nearby parking is available at the Congress and City underground garages. By public transit: just a two-minute stroll from the Golden Roof and Old Town; served directly by IVB tram and bus lines at the Congress/Hofburg and Museumstraße stops.

Tips

The wide gravel paths are completely level and barrier-free, ideal for wheelchairs and strollers. Sit by the swan pond on one of many shaded benches, or stop at the garden pavilion café for coffee and apple strudel. In early spring, hundreds of thousands of blooming crocuses and tulips transform the expansive lawns into a vibrant floral tapestry.
preis: Free admission (Palm House also free of charge)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily year-round from 06:00 to dusk (summer until 21:00)
